h1: The 8 Best Cordless Electric Pruning Shears of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight cordless electric pruning shears, from 1.4 inch budget models to 2.2 inch units, with advice on cut size and batteries.
summary: The SEESII 1.8 inch pruner is the best cordless electric pruning shear: four power modes and a useful 1.8 inch cut for $50 to $100. The 2.2 inch SEESII adds capacity for thick branches, the BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX offers tool-free blade changes, and the two 1.4 inch models are budget picks.
intro: The common pruner mistake is chasing the biggest cutting diameter on the box. A shear rated for 2 inches is rarely needed in a small garden, yet it is heavier in the hand and costs more, while most of what you trim is under an inch. Past the first few weeks, weight, battery arrangement and how well the tool handles thin growth matter more than the headline number.

We ranked eight cordless pruners from spec sheets and owner descriptions. Rated cut diameter, adjustable power modes, battery arrangement, weight and price bucket drove the order. Cut capacity is a ceiling, not a daily setting, so we favored models that match common pruning jobs. Four of the eight state no weight or mode count, and we say so where it affects the pick.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 1.8" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: Four power modes and a useful 1.8 inch cut at a fair price.
products.description:
This cordless pruner has four modes and a 1.8 inch cutting capacity, which covers most shrubs, fruit trees and rose canes. It sells for $50 to $100. Power modes shorten the blade opening for thin twigs and open fully for thick wood, so the motor works only as hard as the branch demands. That saves battery and gives cleaner cuts.

It ranks first because adjustable modes let you match power to the branch, so thin twigs do not get the same hard bite as thick limbs. It sits above the 2.2 inch SEESII because the cut size is enough for most gardens and the price bucket is lower. The tradeoff is a few tenths of an inch of capacity.

Choose it if your branches vary in thickness. The caveat is that very thick limbs still need a saw or the bigger model. Skip it if you regularly cut near 2 inches or thicker.
products.idealFor: Gardeners trimming branches of mixed thickness.
products.skipIf: You regularly cut near 2 inches or thicker.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 2.2" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: The same four modes with the most cutting capacity on the list.
products.description:
A cordless pruner with four modes and a 2.2 inch cut, the largest capacity in this ranking. It sells for $100 to $200. A bigger jaw handles old fruit-tree wood and overgrown hedges that a 1.8 inch tool would stall on, though the motor draws more current for those cuts.

It ranks below the 1.8 inch version because the extra capacity costs a bucket more, and most home pruning never needs it. It ranks above the 2.1 inch brushless model since the four modes give you control over the cut that model lacks. Against the Kebtek's 25mm, it cuts more than twice the diameter.

Buy it for orchards, overgrown hedges or thick limbs. The caveat is price and the extra bulk that comes with a larger capacity tool. Skip it if your pruning stays under about an inch and a half.
products.idealFor: Orchard owners and anyone cutting thick branches.
products.skipIf: Your pruning stays under about an inch and a half.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX* Cordless Pruner Electric Pruning Shears, 900 Cuts Per Charge, Tool Free Blade Change
products.verdict: Tool-free blade changes on a battery you may already own.
products.description:
This pruner runs on the 20V MAX battery system and lets you change the blade without tools. The listing cites 900 cuts per charge. It sells for $50 to $100. Tool-free blade changes matter because pruners dull from sap and thorns, and a fast swap keeps cuts clean instead of tearing bark.

It ranks third because the listing does not state a cutting diameter, so you cannot compare capacity with the SEESII models. What it adds is easy blade maintenance and compatibility with other 20V MAX tools, which cuts the cost if you own a battery already. Against the CRAFTSMAN V20, it is cheaper but ships without a stated battery.

It suits owners of that platform. The caveat is that the cut capacity is not listed, so check the page before buying for thick branches. Skip it if you need a confirmed large cut capacity.
products.idealFor: Owners of 20V MAX tools wanting easy blade care.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed large cut capacity.

products.name: Electric Pruning Shears, Upgraded 2.1" Cutting Garden Shears with LCD Display, Brushless Motor
products.verdict: A brushless motor and 2.1 inch cut without adjustable modes.
products.description:
A pruner with a 2.1 inch cutting diameter, a brushless motor and an LCD display. It sells for $50 to $100. A brushless motor skips the wearing brushes of older designs, so it tends to run cooler and last longer, and the LCD shows battery level and mode.

It ranks fourth because it offers big capacity at a mid price but no listed power modes. Compared with the 1.8 inch SEESII, you get more cutting diameter and a brushless motor, but less control over each cut. Against the 2.2 inch SEESII, it costs a tier less and cuts 0.1 inch less.

Choose it for solid mid-tier capacity on a budget. The caveat is that the brand is generic, so confirm battery and warranty details on the listing. Skip it if you want adjustable power for small twigs.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting large capacity without paying for modes.
products.skipIf: You want adjustable power for small twigs.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Electric Pruner, 2 Ah Battery and Charger Included
products.verdict: A complete kit for people on the V20 battery system.
products.description:
A pruner on the V20 battery system that ships with a 2 Ah battery and charger. It sells for $100 to $200. A 2 Ah pack is a modest capacity, enough for a morning of light pruning, and the V20 platform lets you share batteries with other Craftsman tools.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives no cut diameter, and the bucket is higher than the 20V MAX option. The included battery and charger are the draw, since you can start without owning other V20 gear. Against the BLACK+DECKER, it adds a charger and battery but costs a bracket more.

Buy it if you plan to build around the V20 platform. The caveat is that cut capacity is unlisted, so verify it before relying on it for thick branches. Skip it if you have no V20 gear and want the lowest cost.
products.idealFor: Owners building out the V20 tool system.
products.skipIf: You have no V20 gear and want the lowest cost.

products.name: Upgraded Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Diameter Cordless Power Pruner with LCD Display
products.verdict: Two batteries for long sessions at a low price.
products.description:
A 1.4 inch pruner that includes two batteries and an LCD display. It sells for $25 to $50. A second battery means you can keep working while one charges, which matters for long sessions among vines or hedges where a single pack would end the job.

It ranks sixth because the cut diameter is modest, but it ranks above the cheapest SEESII since a spare battery removes downtime. That swap is the tradeoff over a single-battery tool. Against the Kebtek, it costs a tier less and cuts a little more, at 1.4 inches against about 1 inch.

It suits long pruning sessions in light-duty gardens. The caveat is the 1.4 inch capacity, which is not for thicker limbs. Skip it if you cut branches thicker than about an inch.
products.idealFor: Long, light pruning sessions on a budget.
products.skipIf: You cut branches thicker than about an inch.

products.name: Kebtek Cordless Pruning Shears 25MM Electric Pruners 880G Lightweight
products.verdict: A light 880 gram pruner for people who tire quickly.
products.description:
A cordless pruner with a 25mm cut and a listed weight of 880 grams. It sells for $100 to $200. Holding a pruner overhead tires the arm quickly, so a lighter body helps anyone with a weak grip or shoulder.

It ranks seventh because 25mm is a small capacity and the price bucket is higher than several better-equipped picks. The light weight is its argument. Against the SEESII 1.8 inch, it cuts less and has no listed modes, so it only wins on weight.

Choose it if hand fatigue is the main concern. The caveat is that there are no listed modes, and the cut is smaller than the 1.8 inch SEESII. Skip it if you want capacity or value for the bucket.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who struggle with heavy tools.
products.skipIf: You want capacity or value for the bucket.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Cordless Pruner for Gardening
products.verdict: The lowest-cost way to try cordless pruning.
products.description:
A 1.4 inch cordless pruner with a straightforward spec sheet. It sells for $25 to $50, the lowest bucket on this list. For trying electric pruning, an entry price lowers the risk of a purchase that ends up in the shed.

It ranks last because it lacks the modes of the larger SEESII models and the second battery of the other 1.4 inch pick. What it keeps is a brand name that shows up across this ranking and the cheapest entry price. Against the dual-battery model, it has one battery and no LCD.

Buy it to test whether you like electric pruning. The caveat is modest capacity and no extras. Skip it if you want modes, extra batteries or large capacity.

whatMatters.detail: Cut diameter is the thickest branch the blades are rated to cut. Pushing past it strains the motor and cracks blades. Check the inch or millimeter figure in the title and match it to your thickest branch. The 2.2 inch SEESII leads, while the BLACK+DECKER and CRAFTSMAN state none.

Modes let you reduce blade travel for thin twigs and open fully for thick wood. This saves battery and gives cleaner cuts. Look for a stated mode count, as on the two four-mode SEESII pruners. Models without modes cut everything at full opening, which wastes energy on small stems and shortens each charge. They also tire the battery on long hedges.

A pruner may include one battery, two, or use a shared tool platform. This decides your downtime and total cost. Read the listing for batteries included. The dual-battery 1.4 inch lists two, and the CRAFTSMAN a 2 Ah pack with a charger. A platform pruner is cheap if you own a battery, but pricey if you must buy the pack and charger. Count that cost in.

A heavier tool tires your hand and wrist, especially overhead. A listed weight such as the Kebtek's 880 grams helps compare. Check for a weight figure, and balance it against capacity. Most listings omit weight, so a lighter tool may just be a smaller one. Try the grip with a glove on if you can.

Dull or sticky blades give ragged cuts. Tool-free blade change makes cleaning and swapping easier. Look for that wording on the listing, as on the BLACK+DECKER, and wipe sap after use. Torn bark invites disease on the shrub you trim. Clean the blades between plants for the same reason.

faq.q: Can electric pruners cut as thick as the rating says?
faq.a: The rating is a ceiling for clean cuts on live wood. Hard dry wood is tougher, so leave margin on thick branches. A 2.2 inch SEESII handles a 2 inch stem better than a 1.4 inch model, which will stall. Stay well under the stated limit for the cleanest results.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Paying for capacity you do not use. Match cut size to your thickest regular branch instead of the largest number. The 1.8 inch SEESII covers most gardens, and extra capacity adds weight and cost you will feel in every cut.

faq.q: Is a brushless motor worth it?
faq.a: It generally means less wear and quieter, more efficient operation. The 2.1 inch brushless model lists it, though other models do not. Brushless often costs more, so weigh the price against how often you prune. A weekend user may not need it.

faq.q: Do these come with a battery?
faq.a: The dual-battery 1.4 inch lists two batteries, and the CRAFTSMAN V20 lists a 2 Ah battery with charger. Check the listing for the others, since the BLACK+DECKER sells for owners of 20V MAX batteries and may ship bare. Buying a pack separately adds to the cost.

faq.q: How do I maintain the blades?
faq.a: Wipe off sap after use and keep them dry. The BLACK+DECKER lets you change the blade without tools, and oiling the pivot keeps jaws moving smoothly. Store them with the blades closed and the battery removed.

faq.q: Can I use these on dead wood?
faq.a: Possibly, but dead wood is harder than live. Keep to smaller diameters than the rating, and expect the 1.4 inch pruners to struggle with dry stems. Switch to a saw for anything dry and thick.

finalTake: Buy the 1.8 inch SEESII for mixed branch sizes, the 2.2 inch for orchards and thick limbs, and the BLACK+DECKER or CRAFTSMAN if you already own a 20V or V20 battery. The Kebtek suits people who tire easily, and the dual-battery 1.4 inch long light sessions. Match the rated cut to your thickest regular branch, not the biggest number.
